study.title: Acupuncture Enhances Dorsal Raphe Functional Connectivity in Knee Osteoarthritis With Chronic Pain
study.study_design: Within-subject pre-post design with between-group comparison (patients with KOA vs healthy controls); resting-state fMRI acquired before and after acupuncture stimulation
study.population: Patients with chronic knee osteoarthritis pain and healthy controls recruited from hospital and local community
study.inclusion_criteria: KOA patients: diagnosed according to the Chinese Guideline for Diagnosis and Treatment of Osteoarthritis (2021 edition); middle-aged and elderly people; recurrent knee pain for nearly a month; morning stiffness ≤ 30 min; bone frictions when physically exercising; pain lasts at least 4 months. HC: recruited from local community.
study.exclusion_criteria: Patients who presented with neurological or psychiatric diseases, poorly controlled hypertension, head injury, or any other conditions that might affect the study were excluded.

extraction_notes.note: Supplementary Table 1 contains detailed VAS scores for individual KOA patients at pre- and post-acupuncture; these values are not reported in the main text and could not be extracted.
Supplementary Figure 1 contains FC map for PAG vs right lingual gyrus comparison; coordinates are reported in main Table 1 but the figure itself was not provided.
Supplementary Figure 2 shows the experimental workflow; not provided in main PDF but referenced.

Exact p-values for correlation analyses (Figure 3A and 3B) are not reported in the main text; only R values are visible in the figure (R=0.42 post, R=0.14 pre for DRPN-putamen; R=-0.06 post, R=0.14 pre for MRPN-cerebellum).
No adverse events section is present in the paper. The paper does not explicitly state that no adverse events occurred.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported in this study.
No sham acupuncture control condition was used in this study. All participants (KOA and HC) received verum acupuncture at EX-LE5.
The paper does not report mean ± SD VAS scores in the main text; individual patient data are referenced to Supplementary Table 1 only.

It is unclear whether healthy controls also received VAS assessments or whether the VAS was only collected from KOA patients. The text implies VAS was only for the patient group ('For the patients with KOA, VAS scores were acquired').

The paper states 'no FC changes were observed between pre-acupuncture and post-acupuncture in two groups' for dorsal RPN in one sentence, but then states 'The FC difference of right putamen was significant between pre-acupuncture and post-acupuncture in patients with KOA.' This appears to refer to the ROI-extracted FC value difference confirmed via Figure 2B, not a whole-brain analysis. These are separated in the extraction.

The figure caption for Figure 2B labels significance as '**' defined as 'p <0.05'; the exact test statistic and p-value for this within-group pre vs post comparison in the KOA group are not reported in text or table.

The paper does not describe whether healthy controls received the same acupuncture protocol at EX-LE5 or a different procedure. Based on context, it is assumed they received the same acupuncture at EX-LE5 but this is not explicitly stated.
Needle type, needle size, insertion depth, operator credentials, and manipulation details for acupuncture at EX-LE5 are not described in this paper.
Global signal regression was not explicitly mentioned as used or not used in the preprocessing pipeline.
The study used resting-state fMRI data from pre- and post-acupuncture periods (not during-stimulation task-fMRI) as the primary analysis. Task-state fMRI was acquired but not reported in this paper.
The paper reports group age as mean ± SD (KOA: 59.13 ± 10.27; HC: 58.53 ± 8.15) but does not explicitly state whether age was balanced between groups.
